subject: Request: temporary P1/P2 SLA variance for Sep 20-21 maintenance
messages:
From: Emilia Park <e.park@acmeinc.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary on-call window variance for scheduled infra maintenance

Hi Jasmine,

Quick note from the Acme ops team: we have a planned migration of our database cluster for the evenings of Sep 20 (00:00–06:00 PDT) and Sep 21 (00:00–06:00 PDT). For the migration windows we expect an elevated incident rate related to connection throttling and degraded tail latency.

Because of the volume, we need to request a temporary variance to the P2 response window and an alternate escalation path. Specifically:
- Allow P2 response to be extended to 90 minutes (from standard 60) for the two maintenance nights.
- Route any P1 flags that appear to be database-only degradations to our on-call DB engineering team first (ops+alerts@acmeinc.com) before escalating to Redwood on-call.

We understand this is an exception to the SLO but it's limited to two nights and helps reduce noise for both teams. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept this variance and what approvals you need from our side?

Thanks,
Emilia Park
Platform Ops | Acme Inc.

--
Acme ops alerting: ops+alerts@acmeinc.com
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Emilia Park <e.park@acmeinc.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Sep 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary on-call window variance for scheduled infra maintenance

Thanks for the heads up, Emilia — and for outlining the exact windows. We can accommodate limited, time-boxed exceptions when both sides agree on routing and an approved SLO exception form is signed.

Proposed approach from Redwood:
1) Approve a temporary P2 response window extension to 90 minutes for Sep 20 and Sep 21 only.
2) Configure a two-step escalation: db-only P1 events will be routed first to ops+alerts@acmeinc.com for triage for 10 minutes; if unresolved or if broader platform impact is detected, Redwood on-call will be paged.
3) Apply a temporary fallback to the Dedicated pool if latency spikes exceed 2x baseline for longer than 15 minutes to prevent client-facing degradation.

We need two things to finalize:
- Signed SLO exception form (I attached a template).
- A short approval email from Acme leadership confirming the routing change and that Acme will accept responsibility for db-first triage during the windows.

Ben/Vanessa/Sean — can you confirm the on-call config (PD escalation, automated route) and whether we need any additional throttling protections in the routing layer? I marked the change as an emergency exception request in the console so we can push the routing quickly once approvals are in.

-Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: slo-exception-form.pdf (SLO Exception template), oncall-routing-diagram.png (draft routing)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Sep 2026 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: Request: temporary on-call window variance for scheduled infra maintenance

Forwarding Acme's request and Jasmine's proposed approach. Notes from infra side:

- We can implement the 10-minute db-first routing via a short-lived policy in Smart Routing. It will check the error-class tag (db.connection / db.latency) and route to ops+alerts for the initial 10 minutes. If the tag changes or additional services fail, escalation to Redwood on-call will be automatic.
- For the Dedicated fallback: we can add a temporary route that moves traffic to the dedicated pool for the Acme account when 95th latency >= 2x baseline for 15+ mins. That requires a config change and a feature flag flip; ops runbook will need to document the flip and rollback triggers.
- PagerDuty adjustments: recommend activating a secondary responder for Sep 20/21 (BenC-secondary) and adding Vanessa as the escalation contact.

Action items for Jaguar on-call (infra):
- Create short-lived Smart Routing policy (expires Sep 22 06:00 PDT).
- Add dedicated fallback flag and test in staging (target complete by Sep 18).
- Prep a rollback playbook and brief Vanessa on the escalation steps.

I'll draft the runbook and attach to the exception request. If you want, I can do the config push once we have the signed form from Acme.

Ben Carter
Director, Infrastructure Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Emilia Park <e.park@acmeinc.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Sep 2026 15:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary on-call window variance for scheduled infra maintenance

Thanks everyone — review complete on my side.

Vanessa (ops lead), I approve the temporary variance under the following constraints:
- Approval limited to Sep 20 00:00–06:00 PDT and Sep 21 00:00–06:00 PDT only.
- Acme signs the SLO exception form and confirms receipt of the rollback playbook.
- Redwood will monitor the dedicated fallback and will escalate to Acme within 15 minutes of flipping the feature flag.

Emilia — if you can reply with a short approval line that confirms Acme accepts the db-first triage and will be available via ops+alerts during the windows, we'll proceed to implement the short-lived Smart Routing policy. Ben — please prepare the config PR and the staging test results by Sep 18.

Approved-by: Vanessa Ortiz, Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
